hints: Look at the three features and ask yourself, which ones are absolutely essential for any cell, whether it is a plant cell or a bacterial cell, to control entry and make proteins?
Remember that both plant cells and prokaryotic cells are surrounded by a wall outside their membrane, even though the wall is made of cellulose in plants and peptidoglycan in most prokaryotes.
walkthrough:
**Start with what every cell must have**

All cells need a cell surface membrane to control what enters and leaves. All cells also need ribosomes to make proteins. So features 2 and 3 are universal.

Think: membrane for control, ribosomes for protein synthesis.

**Check the cell wall in both types**

Plant cells have a cell wall made of cellulose for support. Prokaryotic cells also have a cell wall, just made of a different material, for protection and shape. So feature 1 is shared too.

**Put it together**

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all found in both plant cells and prokaryotic cells, the answer is 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct and well done. Both cell types have a cell wall, a cell surface membrane and ribosomes, so 1, 2 and 3 are all shared.
options.B: Not quite. This misses out ribosomes, but both plant and prokaryotic cells need ribosomes for protein synthesis.
options.C: Close but incomplete. This misses out the cell surface membrane, which every living cell has to control transport.
options.D: Almost there. This misses out the cell wall, but both plant cells and prokaryotic cells have one for support and protection.
